_status: Region 'function' and 'space_effect' are Yenna's text (docs/medical/regions.json, merged by scripts/merge_medical.py). Everything else (metrics, layout, forecast settings) is the app's.
_how_to_read: metrics = daily values judged against thresholds.json (worst wins). key_metric = the one charted and forecast. daily_fields = raw daily fields used for the 'unusual for you' check. live_metrics = VitalsFrame fields judged live. context_metrics = cabin values shown with the region (not used for its status). function = one plain sentence on what this body part or system does (shown under the region name).

regions.label: Brain and mood
regions.function: Your brain controls your thoughts, sleep, reflexes, and feelings.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Isolation, noise and shifted light cycles can disturb sleep and mood on long missions.
regions.space_effect: Isolation and schedule changes can disrupt sleep and increase stress [REF-01]. Fluid shifting to your head can also affect your vision and mental sharpness [REF-02].

regions.label: Heart
regions.function: Your heart pumps blood to deliver oxygen and energy to your body.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Without gravity, body fluids shift toward the head and the heart and blood vessels adapt, so heart rate and its response to standing can change.
regions.space_effect: Zero gravity makes your heart work less, which can reduce its size and strength over time [REF-03]. Returning to gravity can make you feel dizzy because your heart has to work harder to pump blood up to your head [REF-04].

regions.label: Lungs
regions.function: Your lungs bring in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Cabin air is recycled, so carbon dioxide and dust can build up and affect breathing.
regions.space_effect: Dust, floating particles, and high cabin CO2 can irritate your breathing [REF-05]. Fluid shifts can also slightly change how air moves in your lungs [REF-06].

regions.label: Immune system
regions.function: Your immune system fights off germs and keeps you from getting sick.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Spaceflight stress can weaken the body's defences and let dormant viruses become active again.
regions.space_effect: Spaceflight stress, radiation, and altered sleep can weaken your immune system [REF-07]. This makes it easier for dormant viruses to wake up or for you to catch a cold [REF-08].

regions.label: Metabolism
regions.function: Your metabolism turns food into energy and manages your body temperature.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Appetite, fluid balance and body mass often change in flight, so eating and drinking enough takes effort.
regions.space_effect: Spaceflight changes how your body uses sugar and stores fat [REF-09]. You might lose your appetite, making it hard to maintain your body mass [REF-10].

regions.label: Bones and muscles
regions.function: Your bones and muscles give you strength, structure, and the ability to move.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Without weight on the body, bones and muscles get weaker unless the crew exercises every day.
regions.space_effect: Without gravity loading your body, muscles shrink and bones lose density very quickly [REF-11]. Daily heavy exercise is required to prevent major bone and muscle loss [REF-12].

regions.label: Radiation
regions.function: Your body's cells constantly repair themselves from daily wear and tear.
regions.spaceflight_note: PLACEHOLDER: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field the crew receives more radiation, with spikes during solar storms.
regions.space_effect: Space radiation damages your DNA faster than your cells can fix it [REF-13]. High doses increase your lifetime risk of illness and can cause immediate fatigue or nausea [REF-14].

co2_context.text: Cabin CO2 has been high; this can cause headaches and poor sleep.
